from.place: perfect-generation proof: affine base case, where O_X is a perfect generator

title: Affine quasi-coherent derived categories have a perfect generator
statement: If X = Spec(A) is affine [def-pc-scheme], then O_X is a perfect object [def-pc-perfect-complex] of D_QCoh(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] and, for every E in D_QCoh(O_X), E is zero if and only if Hom(O_X[n], E) is zero for every integer n [def-pc-generators].

proof.text: By the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], the functor from D(A) to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) is an equivalence with quasi-inverse R\Gamma(X,-), and it sends A[n] to \mathcal O_X[n]. Therefore zero objects and all Hom-vanishing conditions for the shifts of A are preserved and reflected by this equivalence.

source.place: Tag 06Z0, affine comparison, applied in Tag 09IS

proof.text: The structure sheaf \mathcal O_X is represented on the affine scheme by the degree-zero free rank-one module A, so it is perfect by the definition of a strictly perfect complex. In D(A), maps from A[n] to a complex M identify with the corresponding shifted cohomology group of M; hence all these Hom groups vanish exactly when every cohomology group of M vanishes, which is equivalent to M=0. Transporting this calculation across the equivalence in Step 1 gives the asserted criterion for E.
